# requireLength

<link-summary>Returns the value as a valid array-like length, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireLength() — Returns the value as a valid array-like length, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireLength(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a valid array-like length."
): number;
```

A whole number from `0` up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — the range a `length` property may hold.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                        | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                          | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a valid array-like length."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number` — the same value, typed as a valid array-like length.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                   |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a valid array-like length. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireLength(0); // => 0
requireLength(42); // => 42
requireLength(-1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireLength(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
